To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we developed a method to estimate the depth of laminar electrodes in rat motor cortex by analyzing the polarity reversal of laminar field potentials or the threshold for eliciting movements with anodal versus cathodal intracortical stimulations.
(1) polarity reversal in laminin oscillations is detected at 150.1 µm below the beginning of layer 5 and (2) the threshold for elicitation of movement is 78.7 µm deeper than the polarity reversal.
the polarity reversal method estimates within ±90 µM with 95% CI and the intracritical stimulation method estimates within ±69.2 µM with 90% CI.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of microscale devices for the manipulation of neural activity in the brain.
the development of methods that can be used in vivo to identify the location of electrodes in a layered cortex and thereby facilitate interpretation of the recorded signals.
understanding the relationship between the depth of laminar electrodes in the cortex and their electrical properties, and with developing methods for estimating the depth of electrodes in situ.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the polarity reversal method is more accurate than intracortical stimulations in estimating the beginning of layer 5 of a rat motor cortex.
the intracortically stimulated movement threshold method is more precise and the laminar analysis of oscillations is more reliable for the estimation of laminar electrode location.
the two methods presented in this report are complementary in that they provide an estimate of the location of the laminar electrode within the cortical column with a high degree of confidence.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
both the stimulation and field potential methods provide a good estimation of the electrode location in the cortex.
both methods are capable of estimating the depth of layer V with a 90 µm margin of error and the polarity reversal method is more accurate than the intracortrical stimulation method.
the intracortically evoked movement threshold method can be used to identify the location of the electrode in the rat motor area with a high degree of accuracy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the two methods provide a similar estimate of the depth at which layer IV ends and layer V begins.
the two proposed methods are complementary in that one method is sensitive to the laminar structure while the other is sensitive to the direction of the neuronal elements.
both the polarity reversal and the intracortex stimulation method are able to estimate the location of the electrodes within the rat motor cortex with an accuracy of 90–100 µm.
